text:
ajohnson: Quick heads-up 3 I'm prototyping a tiny 'rollback-gateway' shim to handle tenant-level fallthrough during canary / A-B rollouts. Want design feedback.

maria-chen: Nice. What's the failure model we need to cover? full outage, sustained elevated error-rate, or tail-latency degradation?

ajohnson: Ideally all three. Primary goals: automatic per-tenant switchback to baseline variant, minimal client changes, and audit-friendly events.

ryan: Implementation sketch: a gateway service that evaluates a deterministic policy per request (tenant config, recent latency SLOs, error rates) and returns a routing decision. When it falls back, inject header X-Redwood-Fallback: <reason>.

sasha: How do we prevent cascading fallback storms? If many tenants flip at once baseline could get overloaded. Need per-tenant token-bucket + a global admission gate and graceful throttling.

maria-chen: Also add soft-lease semantics: fallback windows auto-expire unless an operator explicitly extends. Prevents silent indefinite fallbacks.

ajohnson: Decision surface prototype:
```
decision = {
  tenant_policy: enum(allow, opt-out, force-baseline),
  latency_budget_ms: 200,
  error_rate_pct: 2.0,
  sliding_window_secs: 60
}
```
Gateway evaluates every 10s using aggregated metrics.

ryan: On metrics: push per-tenant aggregates (qps, p50/p95, error-rate) into rollout-signals stream. Evaluation must be deterministic and idempotent so we can reconcile.

sam-lee: Ownership question: should rollout controller write desired state to tenant metadata and gateway only read it, or should gateway own transient state (leases) for active fallbacks?

ajohnson: Preferred: rollout controller writes policy + probe configs. Gateway manages ephemeral lease records for active fallback decisions (lease table with TTLs) to avoid thrash and enable timeboxing.

sasha: Can we reuse circuit-service? It already has per-tenant circuits and cooldowns. Gateway delegating to that avoids duplicating backoff logic.

maria-chen: Telemetry: emit an event on every decision with fields [tenant, route, reason, prev_variant, new_variant, trigger_metrics]. Those feed the rollout dashboard and alerting rules.

ryan: Add manual override API: POST /tenants/:id/rollback {duration, reason, meta}. That should create an auditable entry surfaced in console.audit and events.

ajohnson: Edge-case: service restarts -> state drift. Mitigate with TTL leases, idempotent reconciliation, and conservative startup behavior (start in baseline until warmed).

devops-bot: deploy rollback-gateway v0.3 -> success :white_check_mark: (canary -> 10% traffic)

sam-lee: Ops note 3 when enabling, reserve headroom on baseline cluster (20%) and add alert if baseline CPU > 70% after fallback.

ajohnson: Test plan suggestions: chaos test that kills variant nodes and verifies fallback stays bounded + observable; load test simulating 100 tenants flipping concurrently.

sasha: +1 to both tests. Also add a warmup window for newly-failed variants so gateway avoids flip-flopping on transient spikes.

maria-chen: Policy UX: allow tenant-level overrides in UI with clear audit trail and an explanation of why fallback triggered (metrics snapshot).

ryan: Dashboard panels: per-tenant fallback rate, baseline headroom, global fallback storm indicator, and recent decision events. Alerting: page on sustained baseline CPU or sustained fallback rate above threshold.

ajohnson: Next steps: I'll draft short RFC with interfaces (tenant-policy schema, lease table schema, event schema, API endpoints) and a reference impl that delegates circuits to circuit-service. Will post RFC in #eng-platform tomorrow morning.

maria-chen: Please include rollout-vs-dedicated-pool considerations for enterprise tenants (dedicated capacity should opt-out of global fallback unless operator allows).

ajohnson: Good call. Will add a policy flag: dedicated_pool: true -> only allow manual rollback by ops.

sam-lee: I'll own the chaos test harness.

ajohnson: Thanks all. Will ping when RFC is live. :rocket:
